articles_note: english glues no article to a headword, but the vocabulary list carries the infinitive marker on every verb, and a verb left carrying it is a verb no dictionary answers to
audio_note: the backup ships real recordings for most of the deck, so little reaches wiktionary and less still reaches synthesis
inflection_note: english wiktionary states a verb's forms in its headword line rather than in a conjugation table, so the inflection stage has nothing to read and is left off

graded_lexicon.name: efllex
graded_lexicon.note: records where a word appears in graded material, not where it is taught, and is keyed on the headword while cards are keyed on the sense — a floor, not a verdict

definition_openers_note: phrases an english definition wears only to announce a part of speech. english turns a verb into a noun without changing a letter, so these openers are exactly what differs between the two cards, and stripping them is what lets the pair be recognised as one meaning
participle_suffix_note: a noun's definition reaches for the participle where a verb's uses the bare stem, so cutting this ending lets the two match
inflection_endings_note: endings a learner reads straight through, so a sentence's inflected word can be matched against a known base form
grammar_words_note: words an english learner reads without being taught them, so a sentence built from nothing but these teaches nothing beside the word it is chosen for
filler_words_note: words every english definition reaches for, so two definitions sharing only these share no meaning. leans on general vocabulary a sentence does not, which is why it is its own list
